I'm noticing the candidate has broken code fences in several places, like the whitelist script block closing prematurely and leaving the rest of the script as stray prose, plus another stray closing fence after the nmap scan block—these structural breaks would mess up rendering.

I'm also seeing that the candidate uncommented a Placeholder Validation section that was hidden in source with a comment block, exposing content and mislabeled tabs (JavaScript, Rust, Go) that the author had deliberately kept out of view—a meaningful fidelity divergence.

There's also a small edit in the keychain-secrets.sh comment and a fix to the AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY variable name, both minor code drifts I should flag as unwarranted changes since code should stay untouched. Beyond that, many headings and TOC entries remain in English despite the rest being localized, and I'm noticing stale anchor links where translated headings don't match their hash targets.

"#view-open-ports" checks out fine, and the import path adjustment for the locale subdirectory looks consistent with the rules. Checking the prose fidelity more, a few hyphenated Hindi phrases read awkwardly but the meaning holds up, and the image path and credit line both seem correct.

Overall I'd rate mdxPreservation low, around 30, since the code drift and the uncommented section pull technical accuracy down to roughly 65 — this isn't ready to publish yet, and I'd suggest sticking to exact matches for conciseness.
